source.place: Tag 01X5 (divisors-lemma-meromorphic-functions-integral-scheme), part (2): for a quasi-coherent $\mathcal F$ on an integral scheme, $\mathcal K_X(\mathcal F)$ is the constant sheaf with value $\mathcal F_\eta$ (proof omitted there); and the proof of Tag 02OZ (divisors-lemma-regular-meromorphic-section-exists), case (1): '$\dim_{\kappa(\eta)}\mathcal L_\eta=1$'. The form stated here (the invertible case, with the sections over $U$ as an intersection of stalks) is the one the proof of lem-sc-line-bundle-rational-section uses; it is the analogue for $\mathcal L$ of lem-sc-function-field-sections-glue.

proof.text: *Trivializations, and $\eta$ in every nonempty open.* By [def-sc-invertible-module] every $x\in X$ has an open neighbourhood $W$ with an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_W$-modules $\varphi:\mathcal L|_W\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal O_W$; by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] (a morphism of sheaves of modules is $\mathcal O(V)$-linear on each $V$) this is a family of $\mathcal O_X(V)$-linear bijections $\varphi_V:\mathcal L(V)\to\mathcal O_X(V)$, $V\subseteq W$ open, with $\varphi_{V'}(\sigma|_{V'})=\varphi_V(\sigma)|_{V'}$ for $V'\subseteq V$. Call such $(W,\varphi)$ a trivialization; if $U\subseteq X$ is open then $(W\cap U,\varphi|_{W\cap U})$ is again one. Every nonempty open $V\subseteq X$ contains $\eta$: otherwise $\eta$ lies in the closed set $X\setminus V$, so $X=\overline{\{\eta\}}\subseteq X\setminus V$ [def-sc-generic-point], and $V=\emptyset$. In particular every open neighbourhood of a point $x$ contains $\eta$, and the intersection of two nonempty opens is a nonempty open (it contains $\eta$).

proof.text: *$\lambda_x$ is well defined and semilinear over $\rho_x$.* By [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] every element of $\mathcal L_x$ is a germ $\sigma_x$, $\sigma\in\mathcal L(V)$, $V\ni x$ open, and $\sigma_x=\sigma'_x$ ($\sigma'\in\mathcal L(V')$) iff $\sigma|_{V''}=\sigma'|_{V''}$ for an open $x\in V''\subseteq V\cap V'$; since $\eta\in V''$ (step 1) this gives $\sigma_\eta=\sigma'_\eta$, so $\lambda_x(\sigma_x):=\sigma_\eta$ is well defined; likewise $\rho_x(r_x):=r_\eta$. It is additive, and for $r\in\mathcal O_X(V)$, $\sigma\in\mathcal L(V)$ the rule $(r\sigma)_y=r_y\sigma_y$ of [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] at $y=x$ and $y=\eta$ gives $\lambda_x(a\,m)=\rho_x(a)\,\lambda_x(m)$ for $a\in\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $m\in\mathcal L_x$ (represent $a,m$ on a common neighbourhood). For $x\in U$ and $\sigma\in\mathcal L(U)$, $\lambda_x(\sigma_x)=\sigma_\eta=\lambda_U(\sigma)$ by definition.

proof.text: *Stalks of a trivialization.* Let $(W,\varphi)$ be a trivialization (step 1) and $y\in W$. Define $\varphi_y:\mathcal L_y\to\mathcal O_{X,y}$ by $\varphi_y(\sigma_y)=\varphi_{V\cap W}(\sigma|_{V\cap W})_y$ for $\sigma\in\mathcal L(V)$, $y\in V$. It is well defined: if $\sigma_y=\sigma'_y$, then $\sigma,\sigma'$ agree on some open $y\in V''\subseteq V\cap V'\cap W$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], and by compatibility with restriction $\varphi_{V\cap W}(\sigma|_{V\cap W})$ and $\varphi_{V'\cap W}(\sigma'|_{V'\cap W})$ agree on $V''$, so have the same germ at $y$. It is $\mathcal O_{X,y}$-linear since each $\varphi_V$ is $\mathcal O_X(V)$-linear, and the same construction for the inverse family $(\varphi_V^{-1})$ gives a two-sided inverse; so $\varphi_y$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{X,y}$-modules. Since $\eta\in W$ (step 1), $\varphi_\eta:\mathcal L_\eta\to k(X)$ is a $k(X)$-linear isomorphism, and for $y\in W$, $m\in\mathcal L_y$: $\varphi_\eta(\lambda_y(m))=\rho_y(\varphi_y(m))$ (both sides are $\varphi_V(\sigma)_\eta$ for a representative $\sigma\in\mathcal L(V)$ of $m$ with $V\subseteq W$). Also $\varphi_\eta(\sigma_\eta)=\varphi_V(\sigma)_\eta$ for $\sigma\in\mathcal L(V)$, $V\subseteq W$ nonempty open.

proof.text: *Clause 1.* Let $x\in X$ and $(W,\varphi)$ a trivialization with $x\in W$ (step 1). By step 3, $\varphi_x:\mathcal L_x\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-modules, so $\mathcal L_x$ is free with the basis $\varphi_x^{-1}(1)$; as $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is an integral domain [lem-sc-integral-scheme-stalks-in-function-field] (2), hence a nonzero commutative ring, this basis has one element and the rank is one. For $x=\eta$: $\mathcal O_{X,\eta}=k(X)$ is a field [def-sc-function-field], so $\mathcal L_\eta$ is a one-dimensional $k(X)$-vector space.

*Clause 2.* Let $x\in X$ and $(W,\varphi)$ a trivialization with $x\in W$. By step 3 (with $y=x$), $\lambda_x=\varphi_\eta^{-1}\circ\rho_x\circ\varphi_x$; $\varphi_x$ and $\varphi_\eta^{-1}$ are bijective (step 3) and $\rho_x$ is injective [lem-sc-integral-scheme-stalks-in-function-field] (2), so $\lambda_x$ is injective. Let $e$ generate $\mathcal L_x$. Then $u:=\varphi_x(e)$ generates the free rank-one module $\mathcal O_{X,x}$, so $u$ is a unit, in particular $u\neq0$ ($\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is a domain, clause 1); hence $\rho_x(u)\neq0$ in the field $k(X)$ by injectivity of $\rho_x$, so $\rho_x(u)$ is a $k(X)$-basis of $k(X)$ and $\lambda_x(e)=\varphi_\eta^{-1}(\rho_x(u))$ is a $k(X)$-basis of $\mathcal L_\eta$, $\varphi_\eta$ being $k(X)$-linear. Finally $\mathcal L_x=\mathcal O_{X,x}e$, and by the semilinearity of step 2, $\lambda_x(ae)=\rho_x(a)\lambda_x(e)$; so $\lambda_x(\mathcal L_x)=\rho_x(\mathcal O_{X,x})\cdot\lambda_x(e)=\mathcal O_{X,x}\cdot\lambda_x(e)$ with $\mathcal O_{X,x}\subseteq k(X)$ through $\rho_x$.

proof.text: *Clause 3, injectivity of $\lambda_U$.* Let $U\neq\emptyset$ be open and $\sigma\in\mathcal L(U)$ with $\sigma_\eta=0$. For every $x\in U$, $\lambda_x(\sigma_x)=\sigma_\eta=0$ (step 2), so $\sigma_x=0$ by clause 2 (step 5). Thus $\sigma$ and $0$ have the same germ at every point of $U$; the underlying sheaf of sets of the sheaf of abelian groups $\mathcal L$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] is a sheaf on $X$, so $\sigma=0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-sections-determined-by-germs]. As $\lambda_U$ is additive, it is injective.

proof.text: *Clause 3, the image lies in the intersection.* If $\tau=\lambda_U(\sigma)$, $\sigma\in\mathcal L(U)$, then for every $x\in U$, $\tau=\sigma_\eta=\lambda_x(\sigma_x)\in\lambda_x(\mathcal L_x)$ (step 2).

source.place: Tag 01X5 (divisors-lemma-meromorphic-functions-integral-scheme), part (2), proof 'Omitted': written out here for an invertible $\mathcal L$

proof.text: *Clause 3, local preimages.* Let $\tau\in\mathcal L_\eta$ with $\tau\in\lambda_x(\mathcal L_x)$ for all $x\in U$. For each $x\in U$ choose a trivialization $(W,\varphi)$ with $x\in W$ and put $U_x:=W\cap U$, a nonempty open containing $x$ and $\eta$, with the trivialization $\varphi|_{U_x}$ (step 1); put $g_x:=\varphi_\eta(\tau)\in k(X)$. For $y\in U_x$ write $\tau=\lambda_y(m)$ with $m\in\mathcal L_y$; by step 3, $g_x=\varphi_\eta(\lambda_y(m))=\rho_y(\varphi_y(m))\in\rho_y(\mathcal O_{X,y})$. By [lem-sc-function-field-sections-glue] applied to the nonempty open $U_x$ and $g_x$, there is $s_x\in\mathcal O_X(U_x)$ with $(s_x)_\eta=g_x$. Put $\sigma_x:=\varphi_{U_x}^{-1}(s_x)\in\mathcal L(U_x)$; by step 3, $\varphi_\eta((\sigma_x)_\eta)=\varphi_{U_x}(\sigma_x)_\eta=(s_x)_\eta=g_x=\varphi_\eta(\tau)$, so $(\sigma_x)_\eta=\tau$ as $\varphi_\eta$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 01X5 (divisors-lemma-meromorphic-functions-integral-scheme), part (2), proof 'Omitted': written out here for an invertible $\mathcal L$: a section of the constant sheaf $\mathcal L_\eta$ lying in every stalk comes from $\mathcal L$; the case $\mathcal O_X$ on each trivializing open

proof.text: *Clause 3, gluing.* With the notation of step 8, the opens $U_x$ ($x\in U$) cover $U$. For $x,x'\in U$, $U_x\cap U_{x'}$ is a nonempty open (it contains $\eta$, step 1), and $\sigma_x|_{U_x\cap U_{x'}}$, $\sigma_{x'}|_{U_x\cap U_{x'}}$ both have germ $\tau$ at $\eta$; by the injectivity of $\lambda_{U_x\cap U_{x'}}$ (step 6) they are equal. $\mathcal L$ is a sheaf of abelian groups on the site of opens of $X$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], so $\mathcal L(U)\to\prod_x\mathcal L(U_x)\rightrightarrows\prod_{x,x'}\mathcal L(U_x\cap U_{x'})$ is an equalizer [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (1), and there is $\sigma\in\mathcal L(U)$ with $\sigma|_{U_x}=\sigma_x$ for all $x$. Then $\lambda_U(\sigma)=\sigma_\eta=(\sigma_x)_\eta=\tau$ for any $x\in U$ (germs are unchanged by restriction to a neighbourhood of $\eta$). With steps 6 and 7 this proves clause 3.

lean.statement: theorem invertible_module_generic_stalk (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X] (L : X.Modules) [L.IsInvertible] : let η := genericPoint X let lam := fun x : X ↦ TopCat.Presheaf.stalkSpecializes L.val.presheaf ((genericPoint_spec X).specializes (Set.mem_univ x)) let ρ := fun x : X ↦ algebraMap (X.presheaf.stalk x) X.functionField (∀ x : X, Nonempty (Module.Basis PUnit.{u + 1} (X.presheaf.stalk x) ↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk L.val.presheaf x))) ∧ Module.rank X.functionField ↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk L.val.presheaf η) = 1 ∧ (∀ x : X, Function.Injective (lam x) ∧ ∀ e : ↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk L.val.presheaf x), Submodule.span (X.presheaf.stalk x) {e} = ⊤ → (∃ b : Module.Basis PUnit.{u + 1} X.functionField ↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk L.val.presheaf η), b PUnit.unit.{u + 1} = lam x e) ∧ Set.range (lam x) = {τ : ↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk L.val.presheaf η) | ∃ a : X.presheaf.stalk x, τ = ρ x a • lam x e}) ∧ (∀ (U : X.Opens) (hU : Nonempty U), let hη := ((genericPoint_spec X).specializes (Set.mem_univ hU.some.val)).mem_open U.isOpen hU.some.property let lamU := TopCat.Presheaf.germ L.val.presheaf U η hη Function.Injective lamU ∧ Set.range lamU = {τ : ↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk L.val.presheaf η) | ∀ x : X, x ∈ U → τ ∈ Set.range (lam x)})
